actions.name: read_file
actions.description: Read a text file. range selects 1-based lines ("120-200", "120:$", "120:+20", "-50:$" for the last 50); first_chunk starts the read at the first occurrence of that text. Paths are relative to the working directory; paths outside it only where the run's filesystem policy allows.

first_chunk.description: Start the read at the first occurrence of this text (range then counts from there).

path.description: File to read, relative to the working directory.

range.description: 1-based line range: "120-200", "120:$" (to the end), "120:+20" (20 lines from 120); negative numbers count from the end ("-50:$").

actions.name: write_file
actions.description: Write a text file: mode "write" (default) creates or overwrites it, "append" adds to its end, "new" creates it and fails if it exists. Parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the working directory; paths outside it only where the run's filesystem policy allows.

mode.description: `write` (default): create or overwrite; `append`: add to the end; `new`: create, fail if the file exists.

path.description: File to write, relative to the working directory.

actions.name: edit_file
actions.description: Replace the one exact occurrence of old_string with new_string in a text file. Fails when old_string is absent or occurs more than once: include enough surrounding text to make it unique. Paths are relative to the working directory; paths outside it only where the run's filesystem policy allows.

old_string.description: The exact text to replace; it must occur exactly once.

path.description: File to edit, relative to the working directory.

actions.name: shell
actions.description: Run a command in this run's runtime (native) with bash syntax. It starts in the working directory unless cwd is given; it is not sandboxed and runs with the current user's permissions. The command is a child process of this executor: an interrupt or a timeout ends its process group; processes it leaves behind after returning are not managed. Waits up to wait_ms (default 30s, max 30 min) for the command to finish; a command still running then continues as a task and this call returns its task_id with the output so far — follow up with `wait_task` / `get_task_state`. Raise wait_ms for commands you expect to take long (builds, tests). Start a long-lived service with nohup / setsid and return at once; on Unix, processes started with `&` / nohup in the foreground command's process group also end when that command is interrupted or times out. Long output keeps its beginning and end.

cwd.description: Working directory, relative to or within the configured workspace. Defaults to the workspace.

wait_ms.description: How long this call waits in milliseconds before the command continues as a task (default 30000, max 1800000).

actions.name: wait_task
actions.description: Wait for a task to finish and return its result, or its current state and new output when wait_ms (default 30s) passes first. A wait longer than 30 minutes is only possible when the session can suspend; otherwise it is capped. Waiting never affects the task.

task_id.description: task id from an earlier result

wait_ms.description: How long to wait in milliseconds (default 30000).

actions.name: get_task_state
actions.description: Return a task's current state at once: its result when finished, otherwise how long it has run and the tail of its output.

task_id.description: task id from an earlier result

actions.name: cancel_task
actions.description: Stop a running task. Only tasks that declared themselves cancellable can be stopped; others report that cancellation is unsupported and keep running.

task_id.description: task id from an earlier result
